newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi Aramco appoints new key oil officials.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Aramco appoints new key oil officials.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's state-owned oil firm Saudi Aramco has appointed five new senior managers, the English language Arab News newspaper reported on Sunday.

Abdul Aziz al-Khayyal is now Aramco's vice president of sales and marketing which gives him effective day to day responsibility for selling the company's near seven million barrels per day (bpd) of crude and refined product exports.
Khayyal was previously the director of sales and marketing in Dhahran and president of Petron Corp in the Philippines, a Saudi-Philippine downstream joint venture.

Other vice president appointments were Ibrahim al-Mishari as vice president of corporate planning, Dhaifallah al-Otaibi at the Ras Tanura refinery, Abdul Rahman al-Wuhaib at project management and Fouad Saleh at community service.
Mishari was previously executive director of corporate planning and Otaibi president and chief executive officer of Vela International Marine, Aramco's shipping arm.
The appointments were made by the company's board of directors which met on November 2 under the chairmanship of the country's Oil Minister Ali bin Ibrahim al-Nuaimi, Arab News reported.
